gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much GPS a week each watch can take and still last 14 days. On the Active Max's 658 mAh battery, the5krunner's roughly 40 h measured GPS run leaves room for about 8.8 GPS hours a week before it falls under two weeks. The Bip 6 is rated at exactly 14 days, so it has none to spare (14/14 = 1.00×).
standout_why: I read our own current page (dealectric.com, 2026-11-08). It lists only rated days (25 days, 13 heavy; 14 days, 6 heavy) and says outright that it has no derived figure. ChatGPT's three answers say only that the Active Max's 25-day rating gives 'a better chance' of two weeks, and they put no number on it. Amazfit's product pages (us/in/uk) returned HTTP 429 every time, and the Tom's Guide page came back as its title only, so I could not check their body text. Going by the titles and snippets, they give rated days, not a GPS-per-week budget. The headroom ratio can be worked out from rated days alone, so a rival could do the same sum. The GPS-hours-per-week figure needs the mAh rating plus a measured GPS runtime, and I did not see it in any result.
decides: It confirms the Active Max as the pick for a strict two-week need. It is the only candidate under $200 with a sourced margin: 1.79× the 14-day target and about 8.8 GPS hours a week on a measured basis. The Bip Max ($99.99, 1.43×) is the budget choice with some margin. The Bip 6 ($79.99) meets 14 days only on its typical-use test pattern; any use beyond that pattern takes it under two weeks.

findings.label: Typical-use drain per day
findings.note: 658 mAh / 25 days = 26.3 mAh/day. Assumes the battery drains evenly through the rated typical-use days.

findings.label: Drain per GPS hour (measured basis)
findings.note: 658 mAh / 40 h = 16.5 mAh per GPS hour. On the 64 h claim it would be 10.3 mAh/h.

findings.label: GPS hours a week that still allow 14 days
findings.note: (658/14 − 26.3) mAh/day × 7 / 16.5 mAh/h = (47.0 − 26.3) × 7 / 16.5 = 8.8 h. GPS is counted on top of typical use, which may already include a little GPS, so this is a ceiling.
